The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 06.12.2016.

The Road Traffic Accident in question took place on 18.08.2016 at about 04:20 PM at Hanuman Setu Yaumna Bazar,
Kashmere Gate, Delhi.
As per the MLC, Babu Lal suffered simple injuries in the said accident.

The said accident was allegedly caused by the vehicle i.e. ForkLift Truck bearing registration No.
HR-55H-9798 which was driven by respondent No.1 Sh. Hare Krishna, owned by respondent no. 2,
Joseph John and insured with respondent no. 3, The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
Brief facts of the case:
2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that the information of an accident was received at P.S. Kashmere Gate vide DD No.32A.

SI went to the spot i.e.

Thereafter, SI reached at the hospital and got to know that the injured had already left from the hospital.
IO collected the MLC of injured bearing no. 230736/16.
Other injured in the present case namely Raju had given the written application to IO mentioning about the accident in question.

On the basis of written application and MLC, the IO had lodged an FIR u/s.
279/337 IPC against the driver of the offending vehicle.
3. Thereafter IO went to the spot of the accident and prepared the site plan.
Notice under Section 133 M.V. Act was issued to the registered owner and driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended and on inquiry, arrested.
Since the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds.
The offending vehicle was seized by the IO and sent to Malkhana.
Mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle and vehicle of the injured was got conducted.
The RC and insurance of the offending vehicle were taken into the custody of the IO.
The documents pertaining to the offending vehicle were found to be correct after verification from the concerned authority.

IO had deposited the MLC for the final opinion of the doctor and further collected the MLC of the injured after final opinion and the injury was shown as 'simple' on the MLC of the petitioner/injured.
The IO investigated in the matter.
On the basis of MLC and on completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/337 IPC were filed against the driver Hare Krishna and DAR was filed before the court on 06.12.2016.

4. Reply/written statement has been filed by respondent nos.1 and 2.

ISSUES FRAMED 5.

On the basis of the pleading of the parties, vide order dated 07.07.2022, this Tribunal had framed the following issues:
i. Whether the petitioner Sh. Babu Lal suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 18.08.2016 at about 16:20 hours involving vehicle bearing registration No.HR-55H-9798 driven by the Respondent no. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent no. 2 and insured with the Respondent no.3?
OPP ii.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP iii.
Relief.

FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS 8.

Before delving into the facts of the current case to decide the aforementioned issues, it is pertinent to highlight that it is firmly established in legal precedents that the proceedings conducted before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of an inquiry.

Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287).

sentences.text: In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation.

In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.

sentences.text: 9. Keeping in mind the aforementioned legal principle for adjudicating the present issue, this Tribunal has thoroughly gone through the testimony of the witnesses and all the material available on record.
Also, careful consideration has been given to the arguments addressed by the Learned Counsels for all the parties.

Issue No. 1:
Whether the petitioner Sh. Babu Lal suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 18.08.2016 at about 16:20 hours involving vehicle bearing registration No.HR-55H-9798 driven by the Respondent no. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent no. 2 and insured with the Respondent no.3?

OPP The factum of accident:
10.

In this matter, to prove the factum of accident, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and deposed as follows:

Counsel for the Petitioner argued that the accident took place on 18.08.2016 at 4:20 PM when the injured Babu Lal was going to Chauhan Patti, Sonia Vihar, Delhi from Pragati Maidan along with one, Raju on a Motor Cycle bearing no. DL-5SBZ-4002 which was being driven by Raju on his correct side of the road.

He further argued that when they reached Hanuman Setu, Yamuna Bazar, Delhi then vehicle bearing no. HR-55H-9798 being driven by its driver respondent no. 1 at very high speed, rashly, negligently and without caution and without blowing horn forcefully hit the aforesaid Motor Cycle from wrong side.
He further argued that as a result of this forceful hit, the petitioner sustained serious/grievous injuries all over his body.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner further argued that the petitioner was taken to Trauma Centre/Lok Nayak Hospital, Delhi.
He sustained abrasion and injury in his head, left shoulder, left hand, left ear & cheek and all over his body.
Further, the DAR shows that the accident took place and the medical documents on record show that the injured suffered injuries due to the said accident.

Counsel for respondent no. 3 argued that the identity of respondent no. 1 has not been established as the petitioner as PW-1 has admitted in his cross-examination that the driver had fled by the time he could see.

However, the IO has clarified in his chargesheet that after the offending vehicle was identified and upon service of notice under section 133 MV Act, the owner/respondent no.2 had produced respondent no. 1 as the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further, the respondent no.1, who was the driver of the vehicle, would have been the most crucial witness capable of refuting the petitioner's allegations of the occurrence of the accident and rash and negligent driving.
However, he did not step into the witness box.
Thus, adverse inference is drawn against the respondents.

In this regard, reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the cases of Teja Singh Vs Suman & Ors., MAC. APP. 1111/2018 & CM APPL. 52384/2018,
52386/2018, date of decision 06/12/2019; MAC. APP. 428/2018, titled as The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Kamla Devi & Ors, date of decision 08.11.2019 and MAC.

sentences.text: From the DAR, it also stands established that respondent no.2, Joseph John was the registered owner of the offending vehicle and further that the vehicle was insured with respondent no.3, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vide policy no. 271700/31/2016/14393 valid upto 25.03.2017.
The factum of said insurance is also admitted by respondent no. 3.

The injury:
14.
It is mentioned in the DAR that the petitioner/injured had sustained simple injuries in the accident in question.
The MLC bearing no. 230736 dated 18.08.2016 issued by Lok Nayak Hospital shows that the alleged history is road traffic accident.
Also, the nature of the injuries suffered by the injured is shown to be 'simple'.

Although, it is the case of the petitioner that he suffered grievous injury but he has not filed any medical document on record to prove the same while the MLC shows the injuries suffered by him to be simple.
Further, the discharge summary shows that the petitioner was discharged from the hospital on the same day.
The petitioner (PW-1) has also admitted same day discharge in his cross-examination.

15. From the above and in totality of the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to bring on record sufficient facts so as to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number HR- 55H-9798 by its driver/respondent no. 1 on the date and time of the accident and that due to the said accident, the petitioner sustained simple injury.
Accordingly, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

Issue no. 2:
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
The petitioner is certainly entitled for compensation in view of decision of the discussion on the above issues.

Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases.

In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result Babulal (I)(Fir302/16/K.Gate) vs Hare Krishna (Oic) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164175355/
6 of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).

entities.text: C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
R. D.
Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv).
17.

In view of the above law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in injury cases, award needs to be passed only under heads of medical expenses, loss of earning during treatment period and damages for pain, suffering and trauma.

This is a case where the petitioner has suffered simple Babulal (I)(Fir302/16/K.Gate) vs Hare Krishna (Oic) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164175355/
7 injury due to the accident, hence, this Tribunal now proceeds further step by step to decide the compensation/award under different heads applicable to the present matter in light of above preposition.
Determination of Injuries and Duration of the Treatment:
18.

It would be appropriate to first ascertain the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner/ injured and duration of treatment as they need to be kept in mind while ascertaining the compensation under different applicable heads.
As per the MLC, the petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 18.08.2016 and was discharged on the same day.
Further, the injury suffered by him has been opined to be 'simple'.
There is no other medical document on record to prove further treatment.

Medical expenses:
19.
The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit of evidence Ex.PW-1/A
that he had incurred more than Rs. 40,000/- on his medical treatment, however, in his From XIV, he has claimed medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 20,000/-.
He has also deposed that he has lost his medical bills.

Therefore, although there are no medical bills on record, but considering the nature of injuries suffered by him, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner/ injured must have incurred Rs.
5,000/- on his medical treatment.

Therefore, an amount of Rs. 5,000/- is awarded to the petitioner/
injured Babu Lal towards medical expenses.

Loss of income:
20.

Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Babu Lal claimed that he was working as labour and was earning Rs. 18,000/- per month, but due to the accident in question, he could not work for 6 months and suffered complete loss of earnings during that period.
However, the petitioner has not filed any document to show that he was working as labour or that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

He has not even filed any document on record to show that he suffered loss of income and also, considering the injury of the Petitioner, it does not seem that the petitioner would have suffered any loss of income.
Thus, he is not held entitled to any amount under this head.

Mental shock:
21.
The petitioner/ injured has not claimed any amount under this head.

Pain and Suffering:
22.
The petitioner/ injured has claim Rs. 1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering, however, no justification has been given for claiming such a huge amount.
It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies from case to case.
Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received certain injuries, therefore, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner as mentioned in the Babulal (I)(Fir302/16/K.Gate) vs Hare Krishna (Oic) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164175355/
8 MLC, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

Special Diet and Conveyance Charges:
23.
The petitioner has claimed Rs.20,000/- under the head special diet and conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence on record regarding money spent by the petitioner under these heads.
However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have spent some money under this head.

Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards expenses incurred on special diet and further Rs.5,000/-
on expenses incurred on conveyance charges.

Attendant charges:
24.
The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 20,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record for the money spent by the petitioner upon an attendant.
However, taking into account the injuries suffered by him, Rs. 5,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of attendant charges.

31.

The offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Hare Krishna, owned by respondent no.2, Joseph John and insured with respondent no. 3, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
32.

This being so, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 argued that the insurance company is entitled to recovery rights as respondent nos. 1 and 2 did not have a valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of the accident.
Respondent no.3 examined Ms. Bharti Meena, Deputy Manager, Oriental Insurance Co. who deposed that the offending vehicle did not have a valid permit and fitness at the time of the accident.
She also proved the notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC and postal receipts whereby respondent no. 2 was asked to furnish the permit and fitness certificate but he did not do so.
Respondent no. 2 did not even produce the said documents before this Tribunal.
Therefore, it is held that respondent nos. 1 and 2 did not have a valid permit and fitness at the time of the accident and thus, there is a breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

However, since the present proceedings are beneficial in nature and the insurance policies are for the benefit of the third persons,

33. Respondent no. 3 insurance company is liable to pay the award amount to the petitioner but respondent no. 3 can recover the amount paid from respondent nos. 1 and 2, jointly and severally.
Issue No.2 is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

RELIEF:
34.

In view of the above, the respondent no. 3 Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. is directed to deposit a sum of Rs. 30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand) along with interest @ 6 % from the date of filing of DAR i.e. from 06.12.2016 till realization with the Civil Nazir of this Tribunal within 30 days under intimation to the claimants, failing which insurance company shall be liable to pay interest @ 7.5 % per annum for the period of delay beyond 30 days.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287).
In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation.
In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.
APP. 690/2017 & CM APPL.
28108/2017, titled as Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Mona & Ors., date of decision 15.10.2019, which had relied upon the judgment in the case of Cholamandalam Insurance Co. Ltd.
Vs Kamlesh 2009(3) AD Delhi 310.
No convincing material has been brought on record by the respondents to show that no accident took place or that respondent no. 1 was not rash and negligent while driving the offending vehicle.
13. It is settled law that this Tribunal is holding an inquiry and not a trial where the case has to be decided to the hilt.
Therefore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/337 IPC and other Babulal (I)(Fir302/16/K.Gate) vs Hare Krishna (Oic) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164175355/
5 relevant documents against the respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no. 1 Hare Krishna (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
15. From the above and in totality of the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to bring on record sufficient facts so as to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number HR- 55H-9798 by its driver/respondent no. 1 on the date and time of the accident and that due to the said accident, the petitioner sustained simple injury.
In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
This is a case where the petitioner has suffered simple Babulal (I)(Fir302/16/K.Gate) vs Hare Krishna (Oic) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164175355/
7 injury due to the accident, hence, this Tribunal now proceeds further step by step to decide the compensation/award under different heads applicable to the present matter in light of above preposition.
Determination of Injuries and Duration of the Treatment:
18.
It would be appropriate to first ascertain the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner/ injured and duration of treatment as they need to be kept in mind while ascertaining the compensation under different applicable heads.
It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies from case to case.
Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received certain injuries, therefore, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries.
Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner as mentioned in the Babulal (I)(Fir302/16/K.Gate) vs Hare Krishna (Oic) on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164175355/
8 MLC, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
In the case of Benson George V. Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. in Civil Appeal No. 1540 of 2022 decided on 25.02.2022, Hon'ble Supreme Court had awarded an interest of 6% per annum.
